brief: Bad vs Good vs Great agents — observability, evals, fallbacks compared side by side.

slots.body: Bad agents log to console and pray. Good agents write structured events. Great agents emit distributed traces with full context replay.
slots.note: Use OpenTelemetry. Your future self will thank you.

slots.body: Bad agents ship on vibes. Good agents run static unit tests. Great agents measure task-completion rates on live traffic with automatic regression gates.
slots.note: Evals are not QA. They are the product.

slots.body: Bad agents throw opaque errors. Good agents retry with backoff. Great agents degrade scope, preserve state, and escalate to humans with full context.
slots.note: Fallbacks are features, not bugs to hide.

slots.body: Bad agents hide inside a black box. Good agents print intermediate steps. Great agents expose checkpointed states you can replay at any node.
slots.note: If you cannot replay it, you cannot fix it.

slots.body: Bad agents change prompts in production. Good agents run offline benchmarks. Great agents shadow-test new chains against live traffic without user impact.
slots.note: Shadow mode is the only honest A/B test.

slots.body: Bad agents pretend to be autonomous. Good agents ask for help occasionally. Great agents route uncertainty to reviewers and learn from every correction.
slots.note: The best agents know when they do not know.

slots.body: Great agents are not luck. They are observable, evaluated, and resilient by design. Start with one layer tomorrow.
